To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The computational cost of part based object detection is dominated by the cost to match each part to the object and not by the optimal configuration of parts.

the cost of part based object detection is dominated by the cost part-to-image comparisons, and not by that of computing the optimal part placement, and that this cost can be dramatically reduced by a coarse-to-fine search procedure.

the cost of object detection is dominated by the cost to compute part-to-image matches, that this cost can be reduced by a coarse-to-fine hierarchical search, that a cascade of hierarchical part models can be trained, and that a combination of these techniques leads to a significant speedup of object detection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new paradigm in object detection, where the focus of optimization is shifted away from the configuration space to the image space.
the problem of fast object detection with part-based models.
the development of efficient methods for deformable object detection and recognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is the best choice for fast object detection with part-based models.

the proposed coarse-to-fine method is the most efficient and effective way to speed up deformable object detection, and the combination of the coarse-to-fine and cascade-of-parts methods is the best way to speed up detection without sacrificing too much detection accuracy.
our method is complementary to the cascades of parts and that it is possible to combine the two methods to obtain very significant speedups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a novel approach for fast detection of deformable objects.
the proposed approach is very effective in speeding up part-based models for object detection, while maintaining the accuracy.
our method is a very fast and accurate deformable object detection method.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cost of matching parts to the image is often the dominant component of the detection cost and therefore accelerating detection by minimizing the number of such comparisons is a very effective strategy.
the computational bottleneck in deformable object detection can be moved from the search for the optimal part placement to the part matching stage.
the computational bottleneck of part based models can be shifted from the matching stage to the training stage, and that this is possible without sacrificing the model's accuracy.
